chunks: Ḥafṣ ibn Ghiyāth narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

Indeed, Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام went out one day with his companions to seek rain. Then he found an ant that had raised one of its legs toward the sky while saying: “O Allah, we are a creation among Your creation; we have no independence from Your provision, so do not destroy us because of the sins of the children of Ādam.” So Sulaymān عليه السلام said to his companions: “Return, for you have been given rain by other than yourselves.”

key_terms.اللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; a direct form of supplication
key_terms.بَنِي آدَمَ: the children of Adam, meaning humankind
key_terms.رِزْقِكَ: Your provision upon which creation depends
key_terms.نَمْلَةً: an ant, presented here as a supplicating creature

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith of Sulaymān عليه السلام and the ant show the effect of du'a in seeking rain?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd عليه السلام went out to seek rain and observed an ant supplicating to Allah for provision and mercy. The report highlights the power of du'a, the dependence of all creatures upon Allah, and that divine mercy may descend because of the supplication of even the humblest of beings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1490 - Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:

"One day, Prophet Solomon (Sulaiman) (as) went out with his companions to pray for rain (Istisqa). He saw an ant raising one of its legs towards the sky, saying,
'O’ Allah (swt), we are a creation among Your creations. We are not in need of anything except Your provision, so do not destroy us due to the sins of the children of Adam.'
Solomon (as) then said to his companions,
'Return, for you have been granted rain due to someone other than yourselves.'".
